body:
Partial transactional DDL implemented in #3108 wasn't applied to `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX`, leading to this issue.

issue.title: "create unique index" appears to create the index when indexed column has dups

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Try this first in vanilla PostgreSQL:
```
create table t(k int primary key generated always as identity, v varchar);
insert into t(v) values
  ('x'),
  ('x');

create unique index t_v on t(v);
select k, v from t order by k;
\d t
```
It causes this expected outcome:
```
ERROR:  could not create unique index "t_v"
DETAIL:  Key (v)=(x) is duplicated.
```
Following this, `\d t` shows this:
```
 k      | integer           |           | not null
 v      | character varying |           |
Indexes:
    "t_pkey" PRIMARY KEY, btree (k)
```
Now try the same in YugabyteDB v 2.0.11. It causes this outcome:
```
ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "t_v"
```
But  `\d t` shows this:
```
 k      | integer           |           | not null
 v      | character varying |           |
Indexes:
    "t_pkey" PRIMARY KEY, lsm (k HASH)
    "t_v" UNIQUE, lsm (v HASH)
```
This is the bug. However, I can't tell if it's a just metatdata bug. But I'm guessing that it is, and that the index doesn't exists because this:
```
insert into t(v) values('y');
insert into t(v) values('x');
select k, v from t order by k;
```
Silently succeeds and we see that table `t` now has three duplicates of the value `'x'`.
